text: Conceivably, these alterations were mediated by increases in glycogen content because osmosis-promoting properties would be required to maintain the ratio of fluid to proteins and thus preserve the integrity of cellular signaling. Although the study provides evidence that training does in fact promote an increase in intracellular hydration (and, thereby, likely an increase in glycogen stores), what remains unclear is whether training-induced increases in intracellular hydration are specific to bodybuilding-type training or inherent to all types of resistance training. Bodybuilding-type training relies primarily on fast glycolysis to fuel performance, and glucose is the primary energy source.
